item.title: The Evolution of Personal AI Agents: From Summarization to Autonomous Organization
item.description:
How four everyday use cases evolved into an agent-based investment office, and why humans remain in the loop. When terms like SDD, AI PDLC, or HG PDLC are mentioned, ordinary people often perceive these acronyms as distant from real life and belonging to the rigid corporate IT sphere. I will explain through a series of personal experiences (from simple to complex) how these abstract concepts are implemented for personal ideas and projects. Read more

item.title: "Happiness for all, for free, and let no one be left behind"
item.description:
You've probably recognized the quote I used for the title. It belongs to Arthur Barbidge, a young idealist who died on his way to the Golden Sphere in the Strugatskys' "Roadside Picnic." I can't promise to play the role of the Golden Sphere, but the conclusion I've reached after many years of reflection, I believe, can lead to such a result. How to achieve universal happiness...

item.title: RAG bot based on expert materials: how I measured search quality and why hybrid was worse than pure vector
item.description:
The expert asked for a bot that would respond in his voice and only use his own materials: PDF courses, video transcripts, and class notes. If the answer isn't in the materials, the bot should honestly direct the user to the live expert, not make things up. I built such a bot using Python and Telegram, and most of the time was spent not on prompts, but on search: the first live questions revealed that the bot simply couldn't find the necessary material. In this article, I'll explain how the search in this bot works, how I built a test stand for measurement (recall@6 and MRR metrics), why the hybrid search, which everyone recommends, lost to pure vector search for me, and what I had to change when I hit the embedding provider's limits. The client agreed to publication only if names were omitted, so the expert, his materials, and the topic are not named here, and the example questions in the article are my own and have no relation to his texts. The code below is taken from working files, with extraneous parts removed.

item.title: Saving Claude Code Tokens with Event Loop Principles
item.description:
In this article, the author discusses the high cost of using Claude Code's agent teams, particularly the 'leader' agent, which incurs significant token costs due to waiting and context management. To address this, the author developed 'supertick,' a plugin that offloads waiting to a script, thus reducing model-related expenses. The article details the problem, the author's attempts to solve it, the architecture of supertick, its installation and usage, cost analysis, integration with external engines like GPT, and lessons learned.

item.title: I thought SKILLs were a useless waste of tokens until I wrote my own
item.description:
Honestly, I didn't understand why SKILLs were needed for LLM agents. With MCP, it's clear: a useful tool to give LLM access to a database or Figma. The only drawback is that to avoid wasting tokens, it's best not to connect 30 MCP servers at once. And in general, it's better to disable unnecessary ones and connect only those that are truly needed for the task. In this light, SKILLs seemed like useless overhead that devours tokens like crazy. I often saw TikTok rants like: connect this SKILL or a whole bunch of them, and you'll be happy. I immediately thought: if I connect them all, subscription limits will run out not by lunch, but by morning. Read more
